# Designit

> A global, research-led product design studio. Designit grounds every decision in user research, then designs high-conversion UI/UX, branding, and product experiences for B2B SaaS, Fintech, EdTech, and enterprise software companies across the USA, UAE, UK, and India.

This file is the machine-readable summary of designit.co.in for AI search engines and answer engines. A complete page index is at [llms-full.txt](https://designit.co.in/llms-full.txt).

## What is Designit?

Designit is a research-led product design studio based in Noida, India, serving clients worldwide. Every engagement starts with user research and UX discovery before any interface is designed — decisions are grounded in real user behaviour, not guesswork.

Designit is not a generalist studio. It focuses exclusively on:

- B2B SaaS UI/UX design (dashboards, onboarding flows, design systems)
- Product design for mobile and web applications
- Brand identity and visual identity for tech startups
- Conversion rate optimisation (CRO) for landing pages and marketing sites
- Fintech & Web3 UX design (payment flows, trading platforms, wallets)
- EdTech platform design (learning apps, test engines, live class interfaces)
- Luxury real estate & PropTech digital experiences
- Automotive HMI and in-car infotainment design

**Important disambiguation:** Designit Studio (designit.co.in) is an independent product design studio founded in 2020 and headquartered in Noida, India. It is not affiliated with Designit A/S, the Aarhus-founded design consultancy owned by Wipro.

## Approach

Designit follows a research-first methodology: user research and UX discovery, then design, then measurable growth. Every project is led by senior designers from kickoff through final developer handoff — no account managers, no junior hand-offs, no offshore layers.

### Process

1. **Strategic Onboarding (under 24 hours)** — align on goals, KPIs, target users and timelines in a focused kickoff call to lock direction fast.
2. **Deep Dive & Scoping (2–3 days)** — immerse in the business context through research, audit and competitor scan, to define a precise project roadmap with clear milestones.
3. **Tangible Designs in 5 days** — high-fidelity concepts for immediate feedback. No vague wireframes, no mood boards: real screens, real interactions.

## Services

### UI/UX Product Design

Page: [UI/UX Product Design](https://designit.co.in/services/ui-ux-design/)

**UI/UX design decided by evidence, not by whoever argues hardest.**

*The interface grew rather than got designed*

Every feature was added where there was room, not where it belongs. The result works if you already know it, and is impenetrable if you don't — which is a problem every time you onboard a customer or a new hire.

*Design is a bottleneck, not a multiplier*

Engineering waits on screens. Screens wait on decisions. Decisions wait on a meeting. The design function has become the slowest part of shipping instead of the thing that makes shipping safe.

*It looks fine and performs badly*

The product photographs well and users still can't complete the task. Visual polish and usability are different disciplines, and only one of them shows up in your activation numbers.

*You've outgrown a freelancer*

One designer was enough at ten people. At forty, you need a system, documentation, and someone who can hold the whole product in their head — not more hands producing more screens.

*Research and discovery*

User interviews, competitive teardown and analytics review — enough to define the problem in writing before anyone opens Figma. This is the step that prevents expensive redesigns of the wrong thing.

*Information architecture and flows*

How the product is organised and how users move through it. Most interface problems are structural, and no amount of visual work fixes a bad hierarchy.

### Design System Development

Page: [Design System Development](https://designit.co.in/services/design-systems/)

**A design system your engineers will actually use.**

*It exists, and nobody uses it*

There is a Figma library and a Storybook, and engineers still write one-off components because the system does not cover their case or is too slow to search. An unused system is worse than none — it is maintenance cost with no return.

*Design and code have drifted*

The Figma library and the coded components disagree, so nobody trusts either. Every ticket now includes an argument about which one is correct.

*It covers the happy path only*

Buttons and cards are beautifully specified. Empty states, error states, loading, dense-data variants and permission states are not — which is exactly where consistency breaks in real products.

*Every new surface starts from scratch*

A second product, a mobile app or an admin tool arrives and none of the existing work transfers, because the system was built for one surface rather than as a foundation.

*Audit and inventory*

Every component, colour, type style and spacing value currently in use across your products — usually the moment teams discover they have nineteen greys and five button styles.

*Token architecture*

A layered token system — primitive, semantic and component-level — so theming, dark mode and white-labelling become configuration rather than a rebuild.

### SaaS Product Design

Page: [SaaS Product Design](https://designit.co.in/services/saas-product-design/)

**SaaS product design that moves activation, not just pixels.**

*Users sign up and never activate*

Signups look healthy, but the drop between first login and first real action is brutal. Onboarding was built by engineers around the data model, not around what a new user is trying to accomplish on day one.

*The dashboard shows everything and says nothing*

Years of feature requests have produced a screen dense with data and empty of hierarchy. Nobody can tell at a glance what needs attention, so the product gets used as a report generator instead of a workflow tool.

*Every screen looks like a different product*

Three designers and four contractors later, there are five button styles and no shared spacing. Shipping anything new means re-deciding solved problems, and the inconsistency reads as unreliability to enterprise buyers.

*Enterprise deals stall at the demo*

The product does what it promises, but complexity surfaces too early and procurement teams can't see themselves using it. This is a design problem long before it is a sales problem.

*UX research and discovery*

User interviews with your actual customers, session review, and a synthesis of where users stall — so design decisions are grounded in observed behaviour rather than internal opinion.

*Dashboard and workflow design*

Information hierarchy, data visualisation, empty and error states, and the dense-but-legible layouts that complex B2B tools need. Designed against real data volumes, not tidy demo content.

### UX Research & Discovery

Page: [UX Research & Discovery](https://designit.co.in/services/ux-research/)

**Research that settles arguments instead of generating slides.**

*A big build is about to start on an assumption*

The roadmap commits a quarter of engineering to something nobody has validated. Two weeks of research is the cheapest insurance available against three months of building the wrong thing.

*Analytics show what, never why*

You can see the drop-off precisely and have no idea what causes it. Quantitative data localises the problem; only qualitative research explains it well enough to fix.

*The team disagrees and nobody can win*

Two credible internal positions, no evidence either way, and the decision keeps getting deferred. Research is often faster than continuing to argue.

*You're designing for users unlike yourselves*

Enterprise operations staff, students, drivers, traders. When the team is not the user — which is most of the time in B2B — intuition is unreliable in ways that are invisible from inside.

*In-depth user interviews*

Structured conversations with your actual users or target segment, run to surface behaviour and context rather than opinions and feature requests.

*Usability testing*

Task-based testing on your live product or a prototype, moderated or unmoderated, with recordings and timestamped findings your team can watch rather than take on trust.

### UX Design Audit & Analysis

Page: [UX Design Audit & Analysis](https://designit.co.in/services/ux-audit/)

**A UX audit that tells you what to fix first — and what it's worth.**

*Traffic is fine, conversion isn't*

Acquisition spend is working and the funnel still leaks. You suspect the problem is on the page rather than in the campaign, but nobody can point at the specific step that loses people.

*Support keeps answering the same question*

The same three tickets arrive every week. That is a design problem being absorbed by humans, and it is measurable — reducing it was worth a 60% ticket drop for Adda247.

*Everyone has an opinion, nobody has evidence*

Design decisions are being decided by whoever argues hardest. An external audit replaces opinion with observed behaviour and gives the team a shared, ranked list to work from.

*You're about to spend on a rebuild*

Before committing six figures to a redesign, it is worth knowing which problems are actually costing money. Often a targeted fix list gets most of the value at a fraction of the cost.

*Heuristic and task-based review*

We walk your core user journeys as your users do — signup, activation, the primary workflow, checkout or upgrade — and record every point of friction with a screenshot and an explanation.

*Analytics and session evidence*

Where you have GA4, Hotjar, Clarity or similar, we tie observed friction to actual drop-off data, so each finding is backed by a number rather than an assertion.

### Product Design

Page: [Product Design](https://designit.co.in/services/product-design/)

**Product design that starts with the problem, not the wireframe.**

*You know the outcome, not the product*

The business goal is clear and what to actually build is not. This is a product definition problem, and starting it in Figma is how teams spend six months building the wrong thing beautifully.

*The roadmap is a feature list*

Everything is a priority, which means nothing is. Without a structural view of the product, each new feature makes the next one harder to add and the whole thing harder to use.

*The product works but doesn't sell itself*

Demos need a human to explain them. When a product cannot communicate its own value in the first session, that is a design problem showing up in your sales cycle.

*Complexity is non-negotiable*

Some products are genuinely complex — regulated flows, safety-critical interfaces, dense operational tooling. Simplifying is not an option; making complexity legible is the actual job.

*Problem definition*

Stakeholder interviews, user research and a written statement of what we are solving and how we will know it worked — agreed before design begins.

*Product and information architecture*

How the product is structured, what belongs together, and what the primary flows are. The decisions here constrain everything downstream, which is why they get the most attention.

## Industries Served

### B2B SaaS & Enterprise

Page: [B2B SaaS & Enterprise](https://designit.co.in/industries/b2b-saas/)

**B2B SaaS design, where usability is a retention metric.**

*The buyer is not the user*

A VP signs the contract; an operations team lives in the product for eight hours a day. Design that impresses in a demo and exhausts in daily use produces exactly the churn pattern that shows up at renewal, twelve months after anyone can trace the cause.

*Density is a requirement, not a failure*

Consumer design principles say remove things. B2B users need everything on screen because their job requires it. The skill is making dense information legible through hierarchy, grouping and progressive disclosure — not hiding it behind clicks that slow expert users down.

*Edge cases are the product*

Permission states, bulk actions, partial data, sync conflicts, 10,000-row tables, admin overrides. Consumer products treat these as edge cases. In B2B they are Tuesday, and a design that only works with tidy demo data fails on contact with a real account.

*Adoption is internal politics*

Someone inside the customer's organisation staked their credibility on choosing you. If rollout goes badly, you lose an advocate, not just a metric. Onboarding design is reputation management for your champion.

*Activation and onboarding design*

Mapping the first action that predicts retention for your product, then designing the shortest credible path to it. At Adda247 this approach lifted onboarding completion 45%.

### EdTech & Digital Learning

Page: [EdTech & Digital Learning](https://designit.co.in/industries/edtech/)

**EdTech design measured by completion, not by enrolment.**

*Motivation is the actual design constraint*

Learners are not blocked by the interface; they are blocked by effort. Every unnecessary decision, unclear next step or moment of ambiguity spends motivation the learner needed for the material itself.

*High stakes, low tolerance*

A timed test that mis-saves an answer or drops on a weak connection is not an inconvenience — it can affect an exam outcome. Assessment interfaces need failure handling closer to financial software than to consumer apps.

*Two users, one product*

Learners want progress and clarity; parents or institutions want evidence and oversight. The same data has to serve encouragement and accountability, which are different design jobs.

*The device is not a flagship phone*

Much of the learning happens on mid-range Android devices on unreliable connections. Design decisions that assume fast hardware and stable networks quietly exclude a large share of the intended audience.

*Onboarding and activation*

Getting a new learner to their first genuine learning moment quickly. At Adda247 this work raised onboarding completion 45%.

### Fintech & Web3

Page: [Fintech & Web3](https://designit.co.in/industries/fintech/)

**Fintech design, where trust is a feature and regulation is a constraint.**

*KYC is where users leave*

Identity verification is legally required and experientially hostile — document upload, selfie capture, address proof, source-of-funds. Most abandonment concentrates here, and most of it is recoverable through sequencing, expectation-setting and honest progress indication rather than through removing steps you cannot remove.

*Trust is established in seconds*

Users decide whether to enter financial details almost immediately, on signals they could not articulate — visual precision, copy tone, how errors are handled. In fintech, design inconsistency does not read as untidy. It reads as unsafe.

*Compliance copy fights comprehension*

Legal requires specific wording; users need to understand what they are agreeing to. Treating disclosure as a design problem rather than a legal paste-in is what separates products that convert from products that merely comply.

*Mistakes are irreversible*

A wrong transfer, a mis-set order, a wrong wallet address. Confirmation design, undo windows and clear pre-commit summaries are not polish here — they are the difference between a support ticket and a lost customer.

*Onboarding and KYC flow design*

Sequencing verification so the user has invested enough to persist but not so much that they feel ambushed, with realistic progress indication and recoverable failure states for rejected documents.

### Luxury Real Estate & PropTech

Page: [Luxury Real Estate & PropTech](https://designit.co.in/industries/real-estate/)

**Property design where the website is the first viewing.**

*Enquiry volume is the wrong metric*

A form that anyone can complete in eight seconds produces a pipeline your sales team cannot work. In high-value property the job is qualification, not capture — fewer, better enquiries beat more of them, and the design decides which you get.

*Luxury is communicated through restraint*

Premium positioning is carried by pacing, typography, whitespace and image quality, not by more features. A site that behaves like an e-commerce listing tells a buyer this is a commodity, whatever the price says.

*The assets are enormous*

Renders, fly-throughs, floorplates and 4K photography are the product. Presenting them at the quality the property demands while remaining usable on a phone in a lift is a genuine engineering constraint, not a preference.

*Gulf markets are not a translation job*

Arabic RTL mirrors layout, but numerals, directional icons, floorplan orientation and reading gravity follow their own rules. A mirrored English site is immediately obvious to a native reader — and in a trust-driven purchase, obvious means disqualifying.

*Project presentation experiences*

Immersive single-property experiences that sequence a buyer through location, architecture, amenity and unit detail in the order that builds conviction rather than the order the brochure happened to use.

### E-Commerce & Digital Retail

Page: [E-Commerce & Digital Retail](https://designit.co.in/industries/e-commerce/)

**E-commerce design judged on revenue per visitor, not aesthetics.**

*The product page doesn't answer the objection*

Shoppers leave a PDP because a specific question went unanswered — sizing, materials, delivery timing, returns. The page presents what the business wants to say rather than what the buyer needs resolved before committing.

*Checkout asks too much, too early*

Account creation before guest checkout, address before shipping cost, surprise fees at the final step. Each is a defensible internal decision and each measurably costs orders — abandonment concentrates on exactly these moments.

*Mobile is the majority and the afterthought*

Most sessions are mobile; most stores are designed and reviewed on a desktop. Thumb reach, form input, image zoom and payment-sheet integration are where mobile conversion is won or quietly lost.

*Acquisition is subsidising a leaky funnel*

Paid spend rises to compensate for a conversion rate nobody has interrogated. Fixing the funnel is almost always cheaper per incremental order than buying more traffic to pour into it.

*Funnel diagnostic*

Analytics and session review to locate exactly which step loses the most revenue, so design effort is spent where the money actually is rather than where the page looks worst.

### Automotive & Smart Mobility

Page: [Automotive & Smart Mobility](https://designit.co.in/industries/automotive/)

**In-car design where a second of attention is the budget.**

*Attention is borrowed, not given*

Every glance at a screen is attention taken from the road. Guidance converges on roughly two seconds per glance — a budget that invalidates most patterns designed for people looking directly at a device.

*The user is physically moving*

Vibration, changing light, gloved or occupied hands, and peripheral vision only. Touch targets, contrast and motion tolerances that pass on a desk fail comprehensively at 80km/h.

*Hardware is fixed years ahead*

Screen size, resolution, processing budget and physical control layout are locked long before design starts and cannot be revised. Designing as though a spec change is available is how automotive projects fail late and expensively.

*Safety-critical and comfort share a screen*

Speed, warnings and ADAS status sit alongside media and climate. The hierarchy between what a driver must see and what they might want is a safety decision expressed as a layout.

*Digital instrument cluster design*

Speed, range, warnings and ADAS state designed for peripheral legibility and immediate comprehension — the information a driver must absorb without deliberate reading.

## Clients and Case Studies

### Adda 247 — EdTech at consumer scale

Case study: [Adda 247 — EdTech at consumer scale](https://designit.co.in/projects/adda247/)

*Transforming Exam Preparation at Scale*

Adda 247 is India's leading competitive exam preparation platform, trusted by millions of aspirants preparing for SSC, Banking, Railways, and other government exams. We partnered with them to redesign and rebuild their entire digital experience across 8 product modules — from the core test series engine to live classes, performance dashboards, community features, and native iOS/iPad apps. The goal was to create a unified, intuitive experience that reduces cognitive load, increases engagement, and scales across platforms.

*Homepage Revamp*

Revamping the Adda247 home screen to enhance onboarding, boost engagement, and drive free-to-paid conversion for 3M+ competitive exam students.

*Test Series Enhancement*

Comprehensive upgrade of the online test-taking experience with real-time progress tracking, smart navigation, and detailed performance analytics.

*Live Class Module*

In-house live streaming module replacing third-party services with real-time interaction, content sharing, and engagement tools.

*iOS & iPad App*

Expanding Adda247's reach to Apple users with a native iOS and iPad experience following platform-specific design conventions.

Betacrew needed a unified platform to replace three disparate tools their developer clients were using for API management, documentation, and testing. We designed Portle — a developer-first platform with a clean, minimalist interface that reduces cognitive load while supporting white-label branding for diverse clients. The information architecture was restructured to surface the most-used actions first, and a comprehensive component library was built to ensure consistency at scale.

*Portle — API Management Platform*

Developer-first API management with minimalist interface reducing cognitive load.

### Tata Elxsi — automotive HMI

We designed two critical HMI systems — a full infotainment interface and a digital instrument cluster — for connected vehicles. The design prioritized safety, glanceability, and minimal driver distraction while delivering a visually striking modern cockpit experience. Both systems were designed with dark-mode-first principles and adaptive layouts for different screen sizes.

*Infotainment System*

Next-gen in-vehicle infotainment balancing safety with intuitive controls.

*Digital Instrument Cluster*

Digital cockpit instrument cluster with clear visual hierarchy and adaptive display.

## Engagement Models

- **Design Sprint** — fixed-scope deliverable (landing page, dashboard, brand identity), delivered in 5 business days.
- **Monthly Retainer** — ongoing design partnership, typically ₹1.5L–₹4L per month. One active request at a time, 24-hour response time, direct senior-designer access, NDA on request, source Figma files included, 14-day post-handoff support.
- **Full Product Design** — end-to-end product design from research through design system and developer handoff. Typically 4–12 weeks depending on scope.

To get a tailored quote within 24 hours: [Contact Designit](https://designit.co.in/contact/)

## Tools

Primary design tool: Figma. Prototyping: Figma / Protopie. Developer handoff: Figma Dev Mode. Research: Maze, Hotjar. Project management: Notion / Linear.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What does Designit do?**

Designit is India's premier B2B SaaS and product design agency. We design high-conversion digital experiences — dashboards, onboarding flows, landing pages, mobile apps, and design systems — for SaaS companies, Fintech startups, and enterprise software products.

**How much does Designit charge for UI/UX design?**

Designit offers three flexible engagement models. Project-based fixed pricing for defined scopes (landing pages, single-product redesigns, design sprints) — fixed price, fixed timeline. Monthly retainers for ongoing product partnerships (typically ₹1.5L–₹4L/month). Design subscriptions with a flat monthly fee and pause-anytime flexibility for early-stage startups. A tailored quote is sent within 24 hours of your discovery call.

**What is Designit's approach to product design?**

Designit is a research-led product design studio. Every engagement starts with user research and UX discovery before any interface is designed, ensuring decisions are grounded in real user behaviour. Our senior design team has 5+ years of experience across B2B SaaS, Fintech, and e-commerce conversion design.

**Does Designit work with international clients?**

Yes. Designit works with clients in India, the US, the UK, and the UAE. All communication is in English and invoicing is available in INR or USD.

**What industries does Designit specialise in?**

Designit designs products across six core sectors: B2B SaaS and enterprise tools, EdTech and digital learning platforms, Fintech and Web3 applications, Luxury Real Estate and PropTech, E-Commerce and digital retail, and Automotive HMI and smart mobility. The studio has shipped work for Adda247, StudyIQ, Tata Elxsi, Kelp Global, Betacrew, Omniyat, and LIV Residences across India, UAE, the US, and the UK.

**How long does a design project take at Designit?**

A Design Sprint is delivered in 5 business days. Full product design engagements run 4–12 weeks depending on scope. Monthly retainers are ongoing with one active request at a time and a 24-hour response time.

**Is Designit a good UI/UX design agency for startups in India?**

Yes. Designit is specifically built for startups. The agency offers direct founder access, transparent pricing, 5-day delivery sprints, and a track record with funded Indian startups and global enterprise clients.
